speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain. To narrow down the cause, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context. To differentiate between a stone and a potential malignancy, do you notice any severe, colicky pain that moves to your groin, and have you ever had any blood clots in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Cell Carcinoma

The history of recurrent urinary tract infections combined with gross hematuria and flank pain raises significant concern for urothelial malignancy or renal cell carcinoma rather than a simple stone. Given your age and symptom profile, I need to visualize the kidney immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Kidney_With_Contrast.
